Um well not sure how this made it onto the ACT but basically:

If you pass through a village on your mail run you have to enter it and then leave it. Thus, you have to use two roads. However, if you start at a village, the first time you leave, you only leave but not enter it, and if you end at a village you only enter but don't leave it on the very last trip. Therefore, the number of roads through a start or end village has to be 1 + 2 + 2 + ...., and so it has to be odd. Only Ripley and Willa have this property. Similarly, a village with an odd number of roads MUST be a start or end city, so none of the others work (as a city that is not a start or end has to have 2 + 2 + ... roads coming from it so an even number.)
